thread:
Iris (Design): FYI noticed in compact request cards the corr-id pill, tiny download icon, and the quick action tooltip are all within a 44px tap area. People on touch devices end up triggering downloads when they meant to copy. Anyone seen this? :grimacing:
Ravi (EngRuntime): Yup. We get support pings about accidental downloads. Also the download triggers a full trace snapshot request which spikes our backend if abused.
Maya (Product): Do we have analytics on how often download is used from the compact card vs full detail page? Might affect discoverability tradeoffs.
Iris (Design): Good call. I checked: ~30% of downloads originate from compact cards in the last 30 days. Proposal: remove inline download icon, use a keyboard accessible triple-dot menu for secondary actions, and add a keyboard shortcut to copy the corr-id (e.g., focus + c) with visible hint.
Lee (Accessibility): Shortcut ideas are fine but need to ensure no conflicts with browser / screen reader keys. Also we must provide an alternative activation for keyboard-only users, and announce actions via live region.
Noah (EngPlatform): From an implementation POV we can add a roving tabindex on the card actions. For download I can gate with a rate limiter and server-side debounce, plus show a small toast: "Preparing download..."
Ravi (EngRuntime): Note: the backend snapshot endpoint returns a large payload for long traces. We should pagine or stream the payload and show progress. Also auth tokens should be validated before starting heavy work.
Maya (Product): UX question: if we hide download in the kebab, will users discover it? Maybe keep an affordance on the expanded detail page and add a subtle tooltip on hover in the compact view that says "More actions (D for download)"?
Iris (Design): Mock idea A: corr-id as primary chip with a copy affordance and keyboard hint "focus + C". Kebab after it with menu items: "Copy correlation id", "Download trace JSON". Mock B: keep tiny download icon but add 2-step confirm on first click ("Download trace?" toast with Undo) — less discoverable but prevents accidents.
Lee (Accessibility): I prefer Kebab + explicit labels. For copy action add aria-label="Copy correlation id" and aria-describedby pointing to helper text. Live region should read "Correlation ID copied" as polite. For download menuitem use role=menuitem and label "Download trace JSON, opens in new download".
Noah (EngPlatform): Implementation checklist: ensure keyboard order is corr-chip -> kebab -> menu. Kebab should be reachable with tab, open with space/enter, menu items navigable with arrow keys, Esc closes. Also test with VoiceOver rotor and NVDA.
Ravi (EngRuntime): I'll add server-side protection: per-user rate limit for downloads, and a warning header if trace size > 5MB that requires explicit confirm. We can return a 202 for large exports and provide a polling endpoint for progress.
Maya (Product): Agree on 202 + progress endpoint. That avoids blocking request worker threads. We'll add telemetry: click source (compact vs detail) and whether user confirmed.
Iris (Design): Updated spec I'll post in #design with new mock images: primary corr-chip, kebab menu, copy shortcut hint, and a small help tooltip. Will include variant with 2-step confirm for comparison.
Noah (EngPlatform): I'll own the a11y keyboard behavior and the rate-limit guard.
Lee (Accessibility): I'll run accessibility test plan after the implementation PR: keyboard nav, screen reader announcements, focus outlines, and shortcut conflicts.
Maya (Product): I'll draft a short release blurb and notify support docs for the new shortcut and behavior.
Iris (Design): Great — aiming to finalize mock by tomorrow EOD and tag @Noah @Ravi for reviews. :raised_hands:

notes: Design thread about compact trace card CTA spacing, discoverability, and keyboard shortcuts. Discusses backend export rate limiting and accessibility behaviors. Contains mock variant proposals and implementation checklist.
